The Court made the following ORDER:
1. This Criminal Petition is filed by Petitioner/Accused No.3, under Sections 437 and 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (for short, 'Cr.P.C.') seeking regular bail in Cr.No.382 of 2022 of Mangalagiri Town Police Station, Guntur District, registered for the offences punishable under sections 419, 465, 467, 468, 420, 506, 120B, 471 Korukonda Vijaya Lakshmi Pandit vs The State Of Andhra Pradesh

The Prosecution's case is that A.1, who works as a Home Guard in Guduru, Nellore District, allegedly enticed the Complainant and other unemployed individuals under the guise of offering Home Guard positions for Rs.8,50,000/-.
Leveraging his purported connections with authorities, A.1 obtained an advance payment of Rs.4,00,000/- from the Complainant, deposited in Axis Bank A/c.No.91901008 1368837 on 23.05.2022.
Subsequently, A.1 claimed that A.2, an employee in the D.G.P., Office, would dispatch an official appointment order.
On 21.06.2022, the Complainant received one appointment order confirming his selection as a Home Guard sent via WhatsApp from No.9493081690 to his mobile No.6300252160.
However, it was later revealed that the appointment order was a fake.

As per A.3's instructions, A.9 totally collected Rs.3,15,53,000/- from 50 unemployed poor youth and A.11 collected Rs.2,00,00,000/- from 22 unemployed poor youth by way of bank transactions into the accounts of A.10 and A.11 and some of those transactions took place in the A.4's presence; A.11 transferred Rs.1,11,15,000/- into the accounts of A.4, A.6, A.5, A.7 from his phone No.9610836108 and from the A.10's account and the remaining cash of Rs.88,85,000/-, A.11 directly handed over to A.3; so whenever A.11 send money into A.3's account, she gave Rs.1 lakh per head to A.11 as his commission.
Upon discovering the deception, the Complainant contacted A.1 to request a refund, but A.1 not only declined but also issued threats of severe consequences.

Allegedly, A.1 and A.2 orchestrated a scheme involving the creation of counterfeit appointment orders bearing forged signatures of police officials, through which they defrauded the Complainant and other unemployed individuals.
The Defacto Complainant subsequently filed a report, leading to the registration of a case against the accused concerning the aforementioned criminal activities.

3. Learned counsel for the Petitioner/A.3 submits that the Petitioner is innocent and has been falsely implicated in the case; there is no iota of truth in the allegations mentioned in the report;
there is no direct evidence to connect the Petitioner with the above crime; Petitioner was arrested on 18.01.2024 and since then, she has been languishing in jail; there is no further need for detention of the Petitioner; there is no scope for Petitioner to either tamper with the evidence or influence the witnesses.
4. Learned Assistant Public Prosecutor opposed the grant of bail to the Petitioner on the ground that the investigation was not completed.

sentences.text: 5. I have heard both sides.
Learned counsel on both sides reiterated their submissions on par with the contentions presented in the petition and the report.
Consequently, the contentions raised by learned counsel need not be reproduced.
6. I have perused the material available on record.
7. As seen from the material on record, Petitioner/A.3 was arrested on 18.01.2024 and since then she has been in judicial custody.

8. Learned counsel for the Petitioner points out that in Crl.M.P.No.52 of 2024 of the present crime,
the learned Principal Sessions Judge, Guntur, granted regular bail under sections 437 and 439 of Cr.P.C., to the A.7 on 24.01.2024.

Learned counsel further contends that the facts of A.7 and the present Petitioner are on the same footing; in Crl.P.No.174 of 2024, this Court also granted regular bail to the Accused Nos.9 and 11 on 29.01.2024.

Considering the aforementioned submissions, I have gone through the material placed on record as well as the orders passed in Crl.M.P.No.52 of 2024 and Crl.P.No.174 of 2024.
9.

As seen from the record, the accusations made against the present Petitioner and Accused No.7, 9 & 11, who were granted regular bail by the District Court, Guntur and this Court, respectively are also on the same footing.

The District Court observed in paragraph No.8 of its order that the investigating agency examined nearly 55 witnesses and opined that there is a prima facie material against the Petitioner, but the Petitioner has been in judicial custody since 07.12.2023.
The District Court observed that the material part of the investigation was already completed.

10. Considering the entire material on record and as also most of the investigation might have been completed by this time, the Petitioner's further detention is no longer required to conduct further investigation in this case.
Learned counsel for the Petitioner placed a medical record to show that the Petitioner has been suffering from ailments.
The said fact is also not disputed by the other side.
It seems that jail Authorities also provided medical treatment to the Petitioner.
The Petitioner is a housewife, aged about 59 years.
No antecedents have been reported against the Petitioner.
11. At this stage, the allegations against the Petitioners are subject to the trial's outcome.
The trial is anticipated to take a considerable amount of time.
Bail serves the purpose of allowing an accused to remain free until their guilt or innocence is determined.

It is settled law that mere apprehension that the accused would tamper with the prosecution evidence or intimidate the witnesses cannot be a ground to refuse bail unless the prosecution shows that the accused tried for such tampering/intimidation.
12. The Petitioner's continued preventive custody is based on an unsubstantiated suspicion that she might tamper with the evidence or influence witnesses.

Given the penal provisions invoked viz-a-viz pre-trial custody, coupled with the prima facie analysis of the nature of allegations, and the other factors peculiar to this case, there would be no justifiability further pre-trial incarceration at this stage, subject to the compliance of terms and conditions mentioned in this order.

Given the same,
the Petitioner's release would not cause in any way hampering of investigation as the Prosecution Korukonda Vijaya Lakshmi Pandit vs The State Of Andhra Pradesh on 14 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/149967270/

13. It is not in dispute that the Petitioner has got permanent abode, there is no possibility of fleeing from justice.
As the case of the prosecution is mostly based on the documents, the release of the accused would not cause hampering of investigation.

14. It is pertinent to note that in the same set of facts, as per the orders in Criminal Petition No.174 of 2024, this Court granted regular bail to the Accused Nos.9 and 11 and the learned Principal Sessions Judge, Guntur, has also granted regular bail to the Accused No.7.
Considering the above facts and circumstances and as most of the witnesses are examined, the release of Petitioner/A.3 would not cause hampering of investigation.

15. Given the discussion made hereinabove, without commenting anything on the merits, lest it may prejudice the trial, the present petition is allowed on the some terms and conditions:
i.

The Petitioner/A.3 shall be released on bail on her executing a personal bond for Rs.1,00,000/- (Rupees One Lakh only) with two (2) sureties for a like sum each to the satisfaction of the learned Additional Junior Civil Judge, Mangalagiri.
ii. On release, Petitioner shall appear before the Investigating Officer concerned as and when her presence is required for investigation.

iii. The Petitioner shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case as to dissuade her from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer and shall cooperate with the investigation;

16. It is made clear that the Petitioner shall scrupulously comply with the above conditions and breach of any of the above conditions will be viewed seriously and Prosecution is at liberty to move an application for cancellation of the bail.
However, nothing expressed hereinabove shall be construed as an expression on the merits of the case.
In this Petition, miscellaneous applications, pending if any, shall stand closed.
